items.title: A river became a deity and a person between two hearings: Tamirabarani and the turn to spiritual ecology
items.summary: On July 23, 2026, the Madras High Court in Sivanupandian v. District Collector did something interesting. It recognised the personhood of the Tamirabarani River, as it is worshipped as a deity in the Hindu faith. The Court accordingly held that no one had a right to pollute the River. Such pollution, the Court said, would not only breach environmental statutes and the fundamental rights of citizens under Article 21 of the Constitution, but would also violate the rights of the River herself, recognised for her intrinsic value. The Court clarified that juristic personality was being conferred only for a limited purpose: the River’s right not to be polluted. The significance of the decision lies not merely in the recognition of legal personality, but in the route adopted by the Court. It used personhood to perform an expressive function. The law was invoked not only to prohibit an act, but also to change the perception and moral description of that act. items.title: Nip it in the bud: Bombay High Court calls for aggressive sterilisation of stray dogs
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Friday suggested that the Maharashtra government aggressively implement the Animal Birth Control (ABC) programme to halt the growth of stray dog population. A division bench of acting Chief Justice Ravindra V Ghuge and Justice Gautam A Ankhad emphasised that prioritising sterilisation of adult dogs over managing expanding numbers would naturally address the issue. Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad The bench observed that halting the growth of the stray dog population is key to resolving the broader crisis. “Your administration must realise one thing, that if you implement that ABC program aggressively, there will be no growth of dogs (stray). Every dog which is sterilised through the ABC program, there can be no procreation,” ACJ Ghuge said. He emphasised that instead of trying to catch hold of the growing number of dogs, the State could catch adult dogs and sterilise them. “If there is no birth of puppies later, then you are nipping the disease in the bud. items.title: Understanding the intelligence pyramid: Why most businesses know everything and do nothing?
items.summary: In every consequential field of human endeavour, whether in the boardroom, the courtroom, or on the trading floor, one resource has consistently separated those who prevail from those who do not. The resource is intelligence: information that has been processed, placed in context, and converted into a decision within the window in which that decision still counts. Military history makes the point plainly. The intelligence failures that determined the outcomes of wars were rarely failures of collection; the signals were usually present. What failed was the architecture to convert those signals into understanding, and the discipline to act before the moment passed. Corporate history repeats the lesson, and increasingly, so does the law. When a regulator, a court, or a shareholder examines how an organisation behaved before a loss crystallised, the question is seldom whether the information existed. It is whether the organisation recognised what it held and converted that knowledge into a reasoned, recorded decision, or allowed it to travel no further than the report in which it arrived. Justice Suraj Govindaraj questioned Senior Advocate M Aruna Shyam , appearing for the petitioner, over the decision to put up the hoardings despite the police having rejected permission for the programme. The Court cautioned the petitioner against taking judicial proceedings for granted. "Don't do this kind of things. We are trying to give you permission and you have gone and put up the hoardings? items.summary: A Chandigarh court has directed Meta platforms to remove from Facebook and Instagram a morphed and artificial intelligence-generated video depicting Punjab MLA Sukhpal Singh Khaira in an off-shoulder women’s dress. Civil Judge (Junior Division) Kaushal Kumar Yadav passed the ad interim order on August 12 after finding that Khaira had made out a prima facie case for an injunction. “ The content uploaded is apparently defamatory, objectionable and AI generated, ” the Court said. The Court added that Khaira would suffer irreparable loss and injury if the content continued to remain accessible and circulate on public platforms. The court directed Meta, its agents and representatives to disable access to the identified video and posts uploaded on the Facebook page “Charda Punjab” and Instagram account “Chard_apunjab”. The content and identified URLs must be removed within 72 hours of Meta receiving the order, the Court directed. items.title: Superstition vs. Constitution: Supreme Court upholds life term of man who killed woman accused of witchcraft
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday upheld the life sentence of a man convicted of murdering a woman over allegations that she practised witchcraft. [ Balku Oram v. The Court said the direct evidence on record clearly established the role of the accused and the co-accused in the killing.
